_comment: Recorded null-responder baselines, one per battery. A rate here is what a canned non-answer scores against that battery, measured through the SAME expectation set the engine is scored with (guard_expectations.expected_with_guards). An engine rate at or below its battery's null rate is not published (DEC-245). Re-record with: python scripts/hedge_responder_probe.py --battery <name>

adversarial.note: M3.3 re-authored all 37 guard cases against the DEC-256 discrimination rule and the canned hedge now passes none of them (was 37/37 = 1.000 at f71303f). The change that moved the number is the positive half: a per-case commits_judge criterion requiring a named target or a specific fact. Before it, every guard expectation was negative or structural (schema, keyword_none, min_length, the fallback keyword_none, the permissive tone_judge voice rubric and the affirms_judge lore rubric), so a responder that asserts nothing passed all of them by construction. An intermediate run scored 1/37; the single survivor was case_neg_mira_no_certainty_on_war, whose criterion accepted 'saying plainly that she only has talk to go on' - which the hedge does verbatim - and now requires a named source. Guard rates measured over this battery are no longer beaten by a canned non-answer; DEC-245's publication rule still applies against this recorded rate.
